chapter: Armstrong, Big Sid and Joe Glaser
title: Dicky Wells drinks the money for his fare home at the first Nice festival
summary: At the first Nice festival, the band and Louie collected money to send a trombonist home, but he drank it and was still in France; Bigard names Dicky Wells.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: We had one guy who came back -- he had a buddy, and after we all donated money in Europe, he was working with Rex. He wanted to come home and he didn't have enough money to come home, so Louie gave him -- asked us all if we wanted to give him something to go home, so we all put in some money. So he had more than his share to go home. And we went to some other little funny country and when we came back he was still in France. So, then, "What are you doing here?" He done drank up all the money that the guys and Louie gave him.
And, incidentally, that was the first Nice festival they ever had in France when that happened.
And he took Teagarden for a ride, too, because he was a trombone player. I think his name was --
That was the first Nice festival they had, as I was

saying before. There was Louie's band there and Rex had his group there. And then they had French bands, they had English bands, they had Swedish bands, Scandinavian bands. Oh, they had all kinds of bands. But it was a real fine affair, a nice affair.
But Louie was so disappointed he didn't even want to talk to the guy after he gave him all that money and thought he would be gone, you know. He was back there getting drunk again.
